ledger.note: 95: Cappadocia becomes a client of Rome. The Kingdom of Cappadocia page (reopened 2026-10-19), infobox status: 'Client kingdom of the Roman Republic and Roman Empire (95 BCE-17 AD)', and 'Ariarathes IX deposed, Ariobarzanes I installed with military support from Sulla: 95 BC'. 90: the Roman army arrives and the invasion is withdrawn. The Kingdom of Pontus page (reopened 2026-10-19): 'A Roman army under Manius Aquillius arrived in Asia Minor in 90 BC, prompting Mithridates and Tigranes to withdraw'; 'Cappadocia and Bithynia were restored to their respective monarchs' (opening fragment, no year of its own). The Kingdom of Pontus page (reopened): 'Mithridates invaded Cappadocia once again, and Rome declared war' (no year; it follows the 90 BC withdrawal and precedes the war that the First Mithridatic War page dates to late summer 89), so 90 is a bridging year, as in kingdom-of-pontus L20. Land and king stay Cappadocian (hatched in Pontic colour); the First Mithridatic War page's 'late summer 89' start and Dardanus 85 bound the occupation. Cliopatria has no Cappadocia shape for 87-78: the new keyframe kingdom-of-cappadocia_-87 bridges it.

The First Mithridatic War page (opened 2026-10-19): 'Sulla finally demanded that Mithridates restore the kings of Bithynia and Cappadocia' and 'Mithridates formally accepted Sulla's terms and reconciled with Nicomedes and Ariobarzanes'; the final meeting 'took place at Dardanos on the Troad coast in late summer or early autumn 85'. wars.name: Orophernes' usurpation
wars.outcome: Demetrius I, angered by Ariarathes V's refusal of a marriage with Laodice V, 'brought forward Orophernes'; Ariarathes fled to Rome c. 158 and 'was restored to his throne by the Romans', letting Orophernes reign jointly, then alone. No border change.

wars.name: Revolt of Aristonicus

zones.text: Lycaonia and Cilicia, added to the Ariarathid dominions

wars.outcome: Ariarathes V 'was killed in 130, during the war of the Romans against' Aristonicus; for his help 'Lycaonia and Cilicia were added by the Romans to the dominions of his family'. The Aristonicus of Pergamon page: 'the revolt was eventually quelled by the Roman Republic in 129 BC'.
wars.note: [Fix 2026-10-19] Span 133 (Attalus III's bequest, as in the kingdom-of-pergamon war) to 129 (the revolt quelled, Aristonicus of Pergamon page); the Ariarathes V page dates only the king's death (130). The grant itself is undated; the ledger takes 129.

wars.name: Mithridates VI's and Tigranes' contest for Cappadocia
wars.outcome: Mithridates defeated Nicomedes 'in a series of battles' over control of Cappadocia; Rome interfered twice (95-92) and installed Ariobarzanes I (95). In 92 Tigranes II 'invaded Cappadocia, expelled Ariobarzanes, and gave the land to Mithridates' (First Mithridatic War page; the Kingdom of Pontus page has 91/90); 'A Roman army under Manius Aquillius arrived in Asia Minor in 90 BC, prompting Mithridates and Tigranes to withdraw'.
wars.note: [Fix 2026-10-19] Extended from 95-92 to 95-90 to match the contest_end of 90 in the ledger and kingdom-of-pontus L19; Armenia added as a belligerent (Tigranes). The span 91/90 on the Pontus side is the Tigranes phase only.

wars.name: First Mithridatic War

zones.text: Cappadocia, held by Mithridates from 90 and restored at Dardanus

wars.outcome: Roman victory: 'Sulla finally demanded that Mithridates restore the kings of Bithynia and Cappadocia' and Mithridates 'formally accepted Sulla's terms and reconciled with Nicomedes and Ariobarzanes' at Dardanos in late summer or early autumn 85.
wars.note: [Fix 2026-10-19] The page dates the outbreak to late summer 89 (infobox 'late summer 89-85 BC'). The Cappadocian theatre is the occupation of 90-85 (ledger); the war's Anatolian and Greek zones are on the kingdom-of-pontus and roman-republic dossiers.

notes: Pages are thin on territory: the original five pages gave the kings, three installations and the 25 BC and AD 17 events but no boundary; every other border move is Cliopatria's (confidence 1) with the counterpart read from the neighbouring shape (Seleucid 188, Pergamon 129, Pontus 110/77, Commagene 63). Start: the page puts Ariarathes I's accession in 331 BC and independence in the reign of Ariarathes III (255-220; the Ariarathes III page: 'About 250 BC he was the first ruler of Cappadocia to proclaim himself king', nothing on independence); the dossier starts at Cliopatria's 239 so that it joins the seleucid-empire dossier's 239 loss, and the two early rulers are clipped to 239. A gap-filler could move the birth to c. 250 or 331 with a page that dates independence. [Fix 2026-10-19, after review] (1) Client relation: Rome 95 to 27 BC and 27 BC to AD 17 (infobox 'Client kingdom of the Roman Republic and Roman Empire (95 BCE-17 AD)'), recorded as vassal_start/vassal_end with the suzerain as counterpart, the vassal's own side as in boii and aetolian-league; roman-republic L134 opens its mirror in 90 (should be 95). (2) Pontic events mirrored from kingdom-of-pontus: vassal 101-97, contest 95-90 (kingdom-of-pontus has only 91-90), occupation 90-85; the First Mithridatic War is in wars. The Cliopatria hole 87-78 is bridged by a new keyframe (-87) with the -91 shape. (3) The 126 grant of Lycaonia and Cilicia is dated 129 (revolt quelled 129 on the Aristonicus of Pergamon page; kingdom-of-pergamon L16 has 129), with a new keyframe -129..-127. Pages disagree: Tigranes' invasion 92 (First Mithridatic War) against 91/90 (Kingdom of Pontus); Archelaus 36 (Kingdom page and text) against 38 (his table); Ariobarzanes I 96 (table) against 95. Still page-silent after the fixes (confidence 1): the 239 birth, the 188 gain, the 129 grant, the 110 strip to Pontus, the 77 return, the 63 strip to Commagene, Pompey's 66-63 settlement. Cliopatria's row runs to 22; the dissolve is AD 17. Gazetteer: all names resolve ('Lycaonia', 'Cilicia', Mersin province).
